title: The threat below the waterline in Cambodia and Thailand’s truce
gist: After Hague talks under UNCLOS Annex V, Cambodia and Thailand agreed confidence-building measures on their maritime dispute, but the author argues the non-binding process is vulnerable to at-sea incidents, military rhetoric and arms procurement.

insights.claim: After five days in The Hague the parties agreed confidence-building measures, including restraint in public statements, senior envoys in each other's capitals and a technical working group on delimitation, under a non-binding UNCLOS Annex V conciliation chaired by Katrina Cooper.
insights.speaker: Nory Ly
insights.so_what: Process is constructive but non-binding; next meeting in Kuala Lumpur 24-27 November.

insights.claim: A non-binding process succeeds only when every actor able to wreck it chooses not to, and that list extends beyond the two foreign ministries.
insights.speaker: Nory Ly
insights.so_what: Spoilers in militaries and media matter more than diplomats.
insights.quote: A non-binding process succeeds when every actor able to wreck it chooses not to

insights.claim: Cambodia initiated the conciliation after the Thai cabinet cancelled a 2001 memorandum covering overlapping claims.
insights.speaker: Nory Ly
insights.so_what: Thailand's unilateral cancellation triggered the legal track.
insights.locator: After the Thai cabinet this year

insights.claim: Fishing-boat swarms of 25-30 Cambodian vessels off Koh Kut drew Thai warning shots in February, followed by a Cambodian detention of a Thai boat, and Bangkok has used administrative coercion such as shutting checkpoints and freezing the Joint Boundary Commission.
insights.speaker: Nory Ly
insights.so_what: Facts-at-sea incidents can derail talks and escalate.

insights.claim: Thai military leaders have publicly forecast a third round of fighting after the rainy season, which risks making Cambodian planners conclude the military holds the veto over diplomacy.
insights.speaker: Nory Ly
insights.so_what: Escalation risk window opens around now; watch Thai military statements.
insights.locator: Another risk is the provocation at home

insights.claim: Thailand selected a bidder for a THB16.7 billion (A$708 million) frigate and approved another THB3.5 billion for missiles, artillery and replacement equipment shortly after the Singapore session; where no boundary exists, new capability reads as intent.
insights.speaker: Nory Ly
insights.so_what: Procurement feeds a regional security dilemma; relevant to defence procurement flows.
insights.locator: Military procurement also sends different signals

insights.claim: The Commission can propose a boundary, but only governments with their armed forces, fleets and media aligned can adopt an effective result.
insights.speaker: Nory Ly
insights.so_what: Low odds of binding resolution without domestic alignment.
